newsitem.title: USA: HERSHEY STOCK RISES AFTER GOLDMAN UPGRADE.
newsitem.headline: HERSHEY STOCK RISES AFTER GOLDMAN UPGRADE.

text.p: Shares of Hershey Food Corp rose on Monday after Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez placed the stock on the firm's recommended list.
The stock, which was 1-7/8 higher at 47-1/2 in early afternoon trading, was previously assigned a market perform rating.
In a report, Ghez said she was upgrading the stock because of attractive fundamentals and its underperformance of relative to the overall market.

The analyst said strong confectionery sales volume may result in better-than-expected earnings growth this year, despite dilution of 0.05 to 0.10 a share expected from the company's recent acquisition of Leaf North America from Huhtamaki Oy .
Ghez estimated 1997 earnings of 2.20 a share in 1997, compared with 2.00 a share in 1996. Her 1998 estimate is 2.50 a share.
She said the declining cost of milk, durum wheat and packaging, as well as reduced operating costs, should help Hershey improve margins this year.
Ghez had reduced her rating on Hershey to market performer at the end of September 1996.
